body: The Royal Malaysian Air Force's first FA-50M light combat aircraft, tail number M58-01, touched down at Labuan Air Base on October 30, 2026, as a stopover before moving to its home base at Kuantan in Pahang. Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled Nordin witnessed the arrival, with the aircraft escorted over the base by RMAF Hawk, F/A-18D Hornet and Su-30MKM jets.

The aircraft is the first of 18 FA-50M Block 20 jets ordered from Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI). The manufacturer valued the deal at $920 million when it first announced the transaction in February 2023, while Malaysian officials valued it at close to RM4 billion. A second aircraft was held back because of a technical issue and, according to the Asian Defence Journal, which attended the event, is expected to arrive in Malaysia by November 1, 2026.

The aircraft will be operated by No. 15 Squadron at Kuantan Air Base. Khaled said the squadron now has more than 200 personnel, including 57 core members trained in South Korea: six pilots, six engineering officers and 45 technicians. All six pilots completed flight training on October 21, 2026, and a formal handover ceremony is scheduled for mid-November in Kuantan. Khaled said the RMAF expects to have six FA-50Ms by April 2027, with the rest delivered by early 2028, while the RMAF said in June 2026 that deliveries would be phased through March 2028. The programme is tied to the planned 2028 retirement of the RMAF's BAE Hawk 108 and Hawk 208 fleet; KAI says the Malaysian variant adds air-to-air refuelling and expanded weapons options over earlier FA-50s and will carry RTX's PhantomStrike active electronically scanned array radar. Khaled said the number of FA-50Ms to be stationed at Labuan air base would be determined after the Hawk aircraft are phased out in 2028, and Labuan, off Sabah in Borneo, is set to host some of the fleet. The RMAF's Capability Development Plan 2055 calls for 36 light combat aircraft, double the current order, and Khaled said no decision has been made on whether a second batch would be more FA-50Ms or another type.
en.summary: Malaysia's first FA-50M light combat aircraft, M58-01, has arrived at Labuan Air Base ahead of its Kuantan basing, the first of 18 ordered from Korea Aerospace Industries as the RMAF prepares to retire its Hawk fleet in 2028.
en.title: Malaysia's first FA-50M fighter arrives ahead of Hawk retirement

body: 馬來西亞皇家空軍首架FA-50M輕型作戰飛機於2026年10月30日降落納閩空軍基地，機尾編號M58-01，僅為中途停留，之後將前往彭亨州關丹作為駐地。馬來西亞國防部長Mohamed Khaled Nordin見證抵達，該機由皇家空軍的Hawk、F/A-18D大黃蜂與Su-30MKM戰機護航進入基地上空。
這是馬來西亞向韓國航太工業訂購的18架FA-50M Block 20中的首架；製造商於2023年2月首次宣布交易時估值為9.2億美元，馬來西亞官員則估值接近40億令吉。第二架飛機因技術問題被留置，據出席活動的Asian Defence Journal報導，預計於2026年11月1日前抵達馬來西亞。

該機將由駐關丹空軍基地的第15中隊操作；據Khaled表示，該中隊目前有逾200名人員，其中57名核心人員已在南韓完成訓練，包括6名飛行員、6名工程軍官與45名技術人員，全部6名飛行員已於2026年10月21日完成飛行訓練，正式移交儀式預定於2026年11月中旬在關丹舉行。Khaled表示，皇家空軍預計於2027年4月前擁有6架FA-50M，其餘飛機預計於2028年初交付，而皇家空軍於2026年6月曾表示交付將分階段進行至2028年3月。此計畫與BAE Hawk 108與Hawk 208機隊預定於2028年退役有關；韓國航太工業表示，馬來西亞版本較早期FA-50增加空中加油與擴充武器選項，並將搭載RTX的PhantomStrike主動電子掃描陣列雷達。位於婆羅洲沙巴外海的納閩預定駐紮部分機隊，但確切數量須待Hawk於2028年退役後才決定；皇家空軍的2055年能力發展計畫要求36架輕型作戰飛機，為目前訂單的兩倍，第二批會是更多FA-50M或其他機型尚未決定。
zh.summary: 馬來西亞皇家空軍首架FA-50M輕型作戰飛機M58-01已抵達納閩空軍基地，之後將進駐關丹，這是向韓國航太工業訂購的18架中的首架，皇家空軍正為2028年Hawk機隊退役做準備。
zh.title: 馬來西亞首架FA-50M戰機抵達，為Hawk機隊退役鋪路
